author: louthforever.bsky.social
text: 7/ Greens decimated - potentially losing 75%+ of Dáil seats. O'Gorman fighting for survival in Dublin West. The eternal question: can smaller parties survive government without being "completely battered by the experience"? #GE24 #Vóta24 #Speirgorm

author: louthforever.bsky.social
text: 6/ Real numbers vs Exit Poll surprises: FF emerging strongest (21.3%), followed by FG (20.8%), SF (18.7%). Both FF's strength and SF's position fell outside margin of error. Expect plenty of analysis in coming days. #GE24 #Vóta24 #Speirgorm

author: louthforever.bsky.social
text: 5/ The numbers don't lie: Far-right candidates hitting rock bottom across constituencies. Dublin South-Central tells the story - combined far-right struggling to hit 7%. All that noise, all that propaganda - for what? Ireland stands proud as European outlier. #GE24 #Vóta24 #Speirgorm

author: louthforever.bsky.social
text: 4/ Unwelcome twist: SF's 6% drop - over 20% of their previous vote share. The push for accelerated UI clearly wasn't this electorate's priority. Green Party's vision of the future similarly penalised. Voters focused on immediate concerns. #GE24 #Vóta24 #Speirgorm

author: louthforever.bsky.social
text: 3/ FF/FG combined share of 42% marks historic low for parties that once commanded 75%+ - and notably, it's an aging vote. The unwinding of Civil War politics continues, though perhaps not in the direction many expected. #GE24 #Vóta24 #Speirgorm

author: louthforever.bsky.social
text: 2/ The generational divide in Irish politics couldn't be clearer. SF commanding youth vote (36% of 25-34s), while FG dominates 50+ (peaks at 28% with 65+). These aren't just numbers - they're competing visions of Ireland's future. #GE24 #Vóta24 #Speirgorm
